findings.title: Trailing-wildcard rule drops the character before '*'
findings.impact: For an origin ending in '*', such as "https://api.*", the rule prefix becomes o[:i-1], which is "https://api" and not "https://api.". The documented pattern "https://api.*" then matches unintended origins such as "https://apievil.com". That makes the allowlist wider than configured, which is a CORS security weakness. A rule like "http://x*" would also lose the 'x'.
findings.recommendation: Use the full prefix before the wildcard: `[]string{o[:i], "*"}`. Add tests for trailing-wildcard origins that cover both a matching origin and a near-miss origin.

findings.title: Trailing-wildcard origin rule drops the character before '*', widening allowed origins
findings.impact: For an origin like "https://api.*", the rule is stored as prefix "https://api" and "*". The "." is dropped, so any origin that starts with "https://api" can match, such as "https://apiattacker.com". With AllowCredentials this could let an attacker-controlled origin read credentialed responses. This depends on how the matcher uses the rule, and that code isn't in the bundle. The changed hunk is only line 134, so I can't confirm the defect comes from this change.
findings.recommendation: Use o[:i] to keep the full prefix, including the character before '*'. Add tests showing that "https://api.*" rejects "https://apiattacker.com".
